# Flora

> Flora is a lightweight multimodal brain-encoding model (~14M trainable
> parameters) that predicts fMRI responses to naturalistic video. It maps the
> audio, visual and textual content of a video onto cortical activity over
> 400 Schaefer parcels (fsaverage5, 20,484 vertices) and runs entirely
> in-browser on WebGPU.

This site hosts the Flora project page and a live interactive demo of the
model (predicted cortical movies, true-vs-predicted comparison, in-silico
modality lesions, and live inference on user-uploaded video).

## Links

- [Flora paper (PDF)](https://qaddasd.github.io/Flora/web-demo/main.pdf): official full version, 35 pages (Russian only).
- [Flora RKNP paper (PDF)](https://qaddasd.github.io/Flora/web-demo/mainv2.pdf): science-project version for the RKNP competition, NIS Aktau (Russian only).
- [Live demo](https://qaddasd.github.io/Flora/web-demo/demo/): whole-brain encoding demo running on WebGPU in the browser.
- [Source code](https://github.com/qaddasd/Flora): PyTorch training code, ONNX export and web demo.
- [Model checkpoints](https://github.com/qaddasd/Flora/tree/main/checkpoints): trained weights (best epoch 52, val Pearson r = 0.7278).

## Facts

- Architecture: frozen MobileViT-S (video) + Whisper-Tiny (audio) + MiniLM-L6
  (text) encoders, MoE fusion transformer (8 experts, top-2 routing), gated
  modality pooling, learnable HRF convolution, per-subject FiLM conditioning.
- Best validation Pearson r = 0.7278 (epoch 52); parcel-wise r up to ~0.93 on
  held-out clips; 98.8% of parcels beat a linear ridge baseline.
- Web stack: vanilla JS + Three.js custom shaders + ONNX Runtime Web (WebGPU,
  WASM fallback). No server required.
